queries.details: Details of the insured company in the tech e&o cyber loss run document. Return in Title Case.

entities.criteria: The insured company of the tech e&o cyber loss run.
Customer or account number, if present
The complete address of the named insured.

queries.details: The details of the cyber and e&o claims. The table could span multiple pages, include all of them even with no claims reported. Do not include any data that has vehicle year, make, and model details. Do not confuse policy level information for claims. The claims table will have a consistent data structure and multiple fields. You may need to include previous pages to get the related coverage type for a claim. Return dates in the format: YYYY-MM-DD. Only return values explicitly indicated in the document. Do not infer values.

entities.criteria: The incurred loss.
The paid loss value in the loss run.
The explicit outstanding (o/s) reserves.
The loss incurred date.
The date the loss was reported.
The date the claim was officially closed
The status of the claim, either open or closed. Exclude no claim entries.
The coverage type associated with the claim (e.g. Cyber, E&O). Only return an entry if the coverage type is Cyber/Tech E&O. If unclear, refer to the loss description.
The policy number this claim is related to. A claim is always tied to a policy.
The file name of the source document.

queries.details: Overview of the complete cyber and tech e&o loss run history. Parse EVERY loss run attachment/document provided in the submission (there may be multiple carriers, policy terms, or files), but only include data from Cyber and Technology E&O coverage; exclude any coverage types that are not specific to the cyber line. Aggregate results across ALL qualifying loss run documents combined, not per individual file. If a document's or claim's coverage type is unclear, refer to the loss description to determine it. Return an empty string if a value can't be found. Return dates in the format: YYYY-MM-DD.

entities.criteria: The line(s) of business covered by the loss runs, evaluated across all loss run attachments. Only return an entry when the coverage type is Cyber or Technology E&O. Exclude any coverage types that are not specific to the cyber line (e.g. General Liability, Property, D&O, EPL, Crime, Auto, Workers' Compensation, or non-tech Professional Liability). If the coverage type is unclear or unlabeled, determine it from the loss description before deciding whether to include it.

The date each loss run was created/valued (often labeled 'as of', 'valuation date', or 'run date'). Only consider Cyber and Technology E&O loss run documents; ignore documents for coverage types that are not specific to the cyber line. If a document's coverage type is unclear, determine it from the loss description. If multiple qualifying loss run attachments exist with different creation dates, return the most recent one.

Combine all open and closed claims from the Cyber and Technology E&O loss run attachments into one dataset.

Assign each claim a year using the policy expiration date of the policy period it is listed under: the claim's year is the expiration date's year. Use only the policy expiration year — do not use loss dates,as of date, report dates, or effective dates to assign years. Every claim must be assigned a year; if a claim's policy expiration date is not shown, use the expiration date of the policy section or period heading it appears under.

Deduplicate: claims are the same when claim number, claimant, and policy period all match. If claim numbers are missing, match on claimant plus claim description plus policy period instead. Keep the record from the most recently valued document.

Include only Cyber or Technology E&O coverage types — if unlabeled or unclear, classify from the loss description; exclude anything else.

Select the loss years using this exact procedure:

List every distinct policy expiration year in the dataset, sorted descending.
The first year in that list is the latest year — even if it is in the future or the policy period is still in force. Never skip it.
Take the first three years. If fewer than three distinct years exist, use all available years — even a single year. Never return empty just because the data covers fewer than three years. Do not assume the years are consecutive (e.g., expiration years present 2019, 2021, 2024, 2025 → use 2025, 2024, 2021).

###IMPORTANT: Before summing, verify the selected years include the largest expiration year in the data; if not, redo the selection.

Sum the incurred losses for all claims whose policy expiration year falls in the selected years. Use each claim's total incurred amount; if no incurred column exists, sum all payment components shown for the claim (e.g., indemnity plus legal) plus any outstanding reserves. Produce one combined figure across all attachments — do not compute per-document totals. Return the years used and the total incurred sum. Return an empty string only if the attachments cannot be found or no claims qualify.

Combine all open and closed claims from the Cyber and Technology E&O loss run attachments into one dataset.

Assign each claim a year using the policy expiration date of the policy period it is listed under: the claim's year is the expiration date's year. Use only the policy expiration year — do not use loss dates, as of date, report dates, or effective dates to assign years. Every claim must be assigned a year; if a claim's policy expiration date is not shown, use the expiration date of the policy section or period heading it appears under.

Deduplicate: claims are the same when claim number, claimant, and policy period all match. If claim numbers are missing, match on claimant plus claim description plus policy period instead. Keep the record from the most recently valued document.

Include only Cyber or Technology E&O coverage types — if unlabeled or unclear, classify from the loss description; exclude anything else.

Select the count years using this exact procedure:

List every distinct policy expiration year in the dataset, sorted descending.
The first year in that list is the latest year — even if it is in the future or the policy period is still in force. Never skip it.
Take the first three years. If fewer than three distinct years exist, use all available years — even a single year. Never return empty just because the data covers fewer than three years. Do not assume the years are consecutive (e.g., expiration years present 2019, 2021, 2024, 2025 → use 2025, 2024, 2021).

###IMPORTANT: Before counting, verify the selected years include the largest expiration year in the data; if not, redo the selection.

Count all claims (open and closed) whose policy expiration year falls in the selected years. Produce one combined count across all attachments — do not compute per-document totals. Return the years used and the total count. Return an empty string only if the attachments cannot be found or no claims qualify.

entities.entity: How many years are included on the loss run all in all?
entities.criteria: Count the number of distinct policy/loss years appearing across the Cyber and Technology E&O loss run attachments combined. Only count years from claims/data whose coverage type is Cyber or Technology E&O and exclude any coverage types that are not specific to the cyber line; if a coverage type is unclear, determine it from the loss description. If the same year appears in multiple documents, count it once. Do not assume continuous years and do not include missing years — only count years that actually appear in the data.

entities.entity: Which years are reported in the loss run?
entities.criteria: List the distinct policy years included across the Cyber and Technology E&O loss run attachments combined, deduplicated. Only include years from claims/data whose coverage type is Cyber or Technology E&O and exclude any coverage types that are not specific to the cyber line; if a coverage type is unclear, determine it from the loss description. If a policy term spans two years (e.g., 2019-2020), return only the policy end year (2020). Do not assume continuous years and do not include missing years — only list years that actually appear in the data.

entities.entity: Total Incurred on all years included
entities.criteria: Sum the total incurred across all policy years found in the Cyber and Technology E&O loss run attachments combined. Include only claims/data whose coverage type is Cyber or Technology E&O and exclude any coverage types that are not specific to the cyber line; if a coverage type is unclear, determine it from the loss description. Deduplicate any policy years or claims that appear in more than one document before summing so nothing is double-counted. Return one combined figure, not per-document totals. Return an empty string if it can't be found.

entities.entity: Total Paid on all years included
entities.criteria: Sum the total paid across all policy years found in the Cyber and Technology E&O loss run attachments combined. Include only claims/data whose coverage type is Cyber or Technology E&O and exclude any coverage types that are not specific to the cyber line; if a coverage type is unclear, determine it from the loss description. Deduplicate any policy years or claims that appear in more than one document before summing so nothing is double-counted. Return one combined figure, not per-document totals. Return an empty string if it can't be found.

entities.entity: Claim Count on all years included
entities.criteria: Count all claims across all policy years found in the Cyber and Technology E&O loss run attachments combined. Include only claims whose coverage type is Cyber or Technology E&O and exclude any coverage types that are not specific to the cyber line; if a claim's coverage type is unclear or unlabeled, determine it from the loss description before deciding whether to include it. Count each unique claim once — deduplicate claims appearing in more than one document using claim number, loss date, and claimant. Include both open and closed claims.
